k: _14th of Harvest. Keeper absent from the lamp, second bell to fourth. Keeper at sea in search of the fishing boat Gull's Return, lost with one aboard. — Y.H._
src: '_14th of Harvest. Keeper absent from the lamp, second bell to fourth. Keeper at sea in search of the fishing boat Gull\'s Return, lost with one aboard. — Y.H._'

k: And below it, in a hand that is not quite steady: _Lamp relit at fourth bell. Wren asleep. Did not find him. Do not tell her._
src: 'And below it, in a hand that is not quite steady: _Lamp relit at fourth bell. Wren asleep. Did not find him. Do not tell her._'

k: ...She went out. Keepers never leave the Lantern. She went out after him.
src: '...She went out. Keepers never leave the Lantern. She went out after him.'

k: Corvin flew into the Stormwall and didn't get in the lifeboat. Hal Merrow's last log said she sent him away so he'd live to be brave about something else. He says it turns out to be us. He said it was raining on him specifically.
src: 'Corvin flew into the Stormwall and didn\'t get in the lifeboat. Hal Merrow\'s last log said she sent him away so he\'d live to be brave about something else. He says it turns out to be us. He said it was raining on him specifically.'

k: It is cold here. It is like being inside a closed eye.
src: 'It is cold here. It is like being inside a closed eye.'

k: Stay close. All of you. I don't like how quiet it is.
src: 'Stay close. All of you. I don\'t like how quiet it is.'

k: It is not quiet. Listen.
src: 'It is not quiet. Listen.'

k: _Cass? Cass, the lamp's gone out. It's so dark._
src: '_Cass? Cass, the lamp\'s gone out. It\'s so dark._'

k: That is her voice. My voice. Hers.
src: 'That is her voice. My voice. Hers.'

k: _Don't let go of my hand. Don't let go. Cass, you're hurting—_
src: '_Don\'t let go of my hand. Don\'t let go. Cass, you\'re hurting—_'

k: He was holding on very tightly.
src: 'He was holding on very tightly.'

k: _FATHER! Father, Lysa's still out there! Leave the lamp! FATHER!_
src: '_FATHER! Father, Lysa\'s still out there! Leave the lamp! FATHER!_'

k: That is him. He was twelve.
src: 'That is him. He was twelve.'

k: _...Cass? I can't see you. It's alright. I'll wait. I'm good at waiting._
src: '_...Cass? I can\'t see you. It\'s alright. I\'ll wait. I\'m good at waiting._'

k: She has been waiting for forty years.
src: 'She has been waiting for forty years.'

k: A bedroom, made of memory. A small bed. A shelf of wooden animals. A girl of ten in a white dress, sitting on the end of the bed swinging her feet.
src: 'A bedroom, made of memory. A small bed. A shelf of wooden animals. A girl of ten in a white dress, sitting on the end of the bed swinging her feet.'

k: Oh! You have my face.
src: 'Oh! You have my face.'

k: It looks good on you. You're older. I always wanted to be older.
src: 'It looks good on you. You\'re older. I always wanted to be older.'

k: I am sixteen. Or I appear so.
src: 'I am sixteen. Or I appear so.'

k: I was going to be sixteen. I had plans. I was going to be a sky-pilot. And a baker. Both.
src: 'I was going to be sixteen. I had plans. I was going to be a sky-pilot. And a baker. Both.'

k: Both is allowed. I am learning that.
src: 'Both is allowed. I am learning that.'

k: Is Cass sad?
src: 'Is Cass sad?'

k: Yes. Very. He is trying to bring you back. He has built a whole noon for you to live in.
src: 'Yes. Very. He is trying to bring you back. He has built a whole noon for you to live in.'

k: I know. I can hear him. He sings all the time. It's very loud. It's always the same song.
src: 'I know. I can hear him. He sings all the time. It\'s very loud. It\'s always the same song.'

k: Will you tell him something for me?
src: 'Will you tell him something for me?'

k: Tell him I'm not in the noon. I'm not anywhere. I'm just a memory he's holding too tight. Memories don't grow up. People do.
src: 'Tell him I\'m not in the noon. I\'m not anywhere. I\'m just a memory he\'s holding too tight. Memories don\'t grow up. People do.'

k: And tell him he was a good brother. Tell him the lamp going out wasn't his fault. He always thinks everything's his fault.
src: 'And tell him he was a good brother. Tell him the lamp going out wasn\'t his fault. He always thinks everything\'s his fault.'

k: I will tell him.
src: 'I will tell him.'

k: Lysa pulls the ribbon out of her hair and holds it out.
src: 'Lysa pulls the ribbon out of her hair and holds it out.'

k: Here. For you. Not because you're me. Because I want somebody to wear it somewhere I never got to go.
src: 'Here. For you. Not because you\'re me. Because I want somebody to wear it somewhere I never got to go.'

k: Will you get old? Properly old? With wrinkles and everything?
src: 'Will you get old? Properly old? With wrinkles and everything?'

k: I would like that very much.
src: 'I would like that very much.'

k: Good. Do it for both of us.
src: 'Good. Do it for both of us.'

k: The dark at the edges of the room thickens. Everything the Gloam has ever kept, every forgotten thing, leaning in — wanting one thing more.
src: 'The dark at the edges of the room thickens. Everything the Gloam has ever kept, every forgotten thing, leaning in — wanting one thing more.'

k: _You are made of us. Come home. Be no one again._
src: '_You are made of us. Come home. Be no one again._'

k: No. I have a name. And now I have a present. You cannot have either.
src: 'No. I have a name. And now I have a present. You cannot have either.'

k: I am keeping it. Not as Lysa. As someone who was given a present.
src: 'I am keeping it. Not as Lysa. As someone who was given a present.'

k: I know. I have decided to be a little vain about it. Pip says it is good for me.
src: 'I know. I have decided to be a little vain about it. Pip says it is good for me.'

k: Under Thornwood's roots we met Lysa — what's left of her. She gave Sable her ribbon and asked her to get old, properly old, for both of them. She gave her a message for Cassian. Sable says she'll deliver it.
src: 'Under Thornwood\'s roots we met Lysa — what\'s left of her. She gave Sable her ribbon and asked her to get old, properly old, for both of them. She gave her a message for Cassian. Sable says she\'ll deliver it.'

k: Visitors! Mind the brass. Don't mind the biscuits. Take two, they're mostly raisins.
src: 'Visitors! Mind the brass. Don\'t mind the biscuits. Take two, they\'re mostly raisins.'

k: On the old woman's desk, under the biscuit tin, a brass nameplate: OTTOLINE MARSH, ASTRONOMER.
src: 'On the old woman\'s desk, under the biscuit tin, a brass nameplate: OTTOLINE MARSH, ASTRONOMER.'

k: Ottoline Marsh— you wrote _The Sunward Atlas_!
src: 'Ottoline Marsh— you wrote _The Sunward Atlas_!'

k: Somebody READ it? Ha! That's both my readers in one week!
src: 'Somebody READ it? Ha! That\'s both my readers in one week!'

k: Cassian gave me a copy. Before— everything.
src: 'Cassian gave me a copy. Before— everything.'

k: ...Oh. Well. He always did have excellent taste in books, and dreadful taste in absolutely everything else.
src: '...Oh. Well. He always did have excellent taste in books, and dreadful taste in absolutely everything else.'

k: When the sun broke, the stars came loose too. Only little ones. Starfall. They fell where the light was strongest — into the Lantern ruins, mostly, and the old sea floor.
src: 'When the sun broke, the stars came loose too. Only little ones. Starfall. They fell where the light was strongest — into the Lantern ruins, mostly, and the old sea floor.'

k: I'm rebuilding my chart of the sky so I can see what's coming. I need the fragments. Seven, if my sums are right, and they usually are, except when they aren't.
src: 'I\'m rebuilding my chart of the sky so I can see what\'s coming. I need the fragments. Seven, if my sums are right, and they usually are, except when they aren\'t.'

k: Bring me what you find. I have a great many things I don't need, and one thing I'd very much like to give to the right person.
src: 'Bring me what you find. I have a great many things I don\'t need, and one thing I\'d very much like to give to the right person.'

k: The Drowned Stars
src: 'The Drowned Stars'

k: Ottoline Marsh needs seven Starfall Fragments — splinters of starlight that fell into the Lantern ruins and the Drowned Reef.
src: 'Ottoline Marsh needs seven Starfall Fragments — splinters of starlight that fell into the Lantern ruins and the Drowned Reef.'

k: Look at that sky. Seven little lights where there were none. I'll name one after you. Something dignified. "Wren's Embarrassment."
src: 'Look at that sky. Seven little lights where there were none. I\'ll name one after you. Something dignified. "Wren\'s Embarrassment."'

k: It's still falling, you know. The one that didn't land. The telescope will show you, if you've the nerve.
src: 'It\'s still falling, you know. The one that didn\'t land. The telescope will show you, if you\'ve the nerve.'

k: No starfall yet? Try the old Lanterns. Stars always did like a lighthouse.
src: 'No starfall yet? Try the old Lanterns. Stars always did like a lighthouse.'

k: And something for your trouble. Don't argue. I'm old, I'm allowed.
src: 'And something for your trouble. Don\'t argue. I\'m old, I\'m allowed.'

k: Ottoline sets the last fragment into the great brass orrery. Seven small lights wink on across the dome, and the whole observatory hums like a held note.
src: 'Ottoline sets the last fragment into the great brass orrery. Seven small lights wink on across the dome, and the whole observatory hums like a held note.'

k: There. The drowned stars, back where they belong. Or near enough.
src: 'There. The drowned stars, back where they belong. Or near enough.'

k: You can't put the old sun back, you know. Nobody can. Not the Hierophant, not a hundred Keepers.
src: 'You can\'t put the old sun back, you know. Nobody can. Not the Hierophant, not a hundred Keepers.'

k: But stars are only suns that are very far away. Perhaps the trick isn't to mend the big one. Perhaps it's to make a small one, close by, that belongs to everybody.
src: 'But stars are only suns that are very far away. Perhaps the trick isn\'t to mend the big one. Perhaps it\'s to make a small one, close by, that belongs to everybody.'

k: ...A small one.
src: '...A small one.'

k: It's only a theory. I've written it in the margins of my own book. Nobody reads the margins.
src: 'It\'s only a theory. I\'ve written it in the margins of my own book. Nobody reads the margins.'

k: Now. The thing I wanted to give to the right person. It isn't a thing. It's a way of looking.
src: 'Now. The thing I wanted to give to the right person. It isn\'t a thing. It\'s a way of looking.'

k: Read the sky. Bend fate a little, when it needs bending. Never more than a little. It sulks.
src: 'Read the sky. Bend fate a little, when it needs bending. Never more than a little. It sulks.'

k: ...Oh. Oh, dear. With the chart complete I can see it. One of them didn't land. It's still falling. Toward _us_.
src: '...Oh. Oh, dear. With the chart complete I can see it. One of them didn\'t land. It\'s still falling. Toward _us_.'

k: How fast?
src: 'How fast?'

k: Tonight-ish. Look through the telescope if you're feeling brave. Or foolish. They're the same muscle.
src: 'Tonight-ish. Look through the telescope if you\'re feeling brave. Or foolish. They\'re the same muscle.'

k: Ottoline Marsh finished her map of the drowned stars and taught us to read them. She says you can't mend the old sun — but maybe you can make a small one, close by, that belongs to everybody. I can't stop thinking about it.
src: 'Ottoline Marsh finished her map of the drowned stars and taught us to read them. She says you can\'t mend the old sun — but maybe you can make a small one, close by, that belongs to everybody. I can\'t stop thinking about it.'

k: Through the great glass: seven small lights, and the dark between them, which is not as empty as it looks.
src: 'Through the great glass: seven small lights, and the dark between them, which is not as empty as it looks.'

k: Through the great glass: cloud, cloud, and the faint hum of something very far away. Ottoline's chart has gaps in it.
src: 'Through the great glass: cloud, cloud, and the faint hum of something very far away. Ottoline\'s chart has gaps in it.'
